## You Have Done This Before {.smaller}

::: {.fillable}
| | Claim | The smaller pieces |
|---|---|---|
| HW1 | every WFF has atoms = binary connectives + 1 | |
| HW2 | every expression has a CNF | |
| Towers | every height $n > 23$ can be built | |
: {tbl-colwidths="[12,58,30]"}
:::

Check the smallest cases. Assume the claim for the smaller pieces. Show it
for the whole.

::: notes
HW1: the WFFs a formula is built from. HW2: the two expressions joined by an
and or an or. Towers: the tower of height n - 5.

The name is structural induction when the smaller pieces are parts of the
thing; induction on n when they are smaller integers. Same skeleton. HW2
promised "we will study it formally in a few weeks" -- this is that.

WHERE HW1 USES THE IH -- easy to miss. Write a for atoms, b for binary
connectives; the claim is a = b + 1.
  Atom: a = 1, b = 0. No IH.
  ~A: negation adds neither, so the IH on A gives it directly.
  (A ^ B): a_T = a_1 + a_2 and b_T = b_1 + b_2 + 1. Those two are just
  counting -- true of any formula, no IH. On their own they prove nothing.
  Subtract: a_T - b_T = (a_1 - b_1) + (a_2 - b_2) - 1.
  The claim says that difference is 1. The counting says how the difference
  COMBINES; the IH supplies the pieces' values, a_1 - b_1 = a_2 - b_2 = 1,
  so 1 + 1 - 1 = 1.
  Without the IH nothing follows: a piece with 5 atoms and no connectives would
  leave the whole off by 4. The IH is what rules that out.
"You used the IH without noticing" -- worth saying out loud.

THE CNF PROOF (HW2), same skeleton.
Theorem: for every expression phi there is a CNF psi with phi == psi.
A for-all-exists statement -- L9's nested quantifiers.
After phases 1 and 2 (remove -> and <->; push ~ down to the atoms) every
expression is built from literals with ^ and v. Prove it for those:
  Literal: one clause of one literal. No IH.
  A ^ B: IH gives A == C1^...^Cm and B == D1^...^Dk. Then
         A ^ B == C1^...^Cm^D1^...^Dk, already an AND of clauses.
  A v B: same IH. Distribute: A v B == AND over i,j of (Ci v Dj). Each Ci v Dj
         is an OR of two ORs of literals -- a clause. So a CNF.
Where the IH is used: in both combining cases. Contrast with HW1: there the IH
handed over a NUMBER about each piece (a - b = 1); here it hands over an OBJECT,
a CNF for each piece -- because the theorem is for-all-exists, the IH supplies
witnesses and the step builds the new witness from them.
:::

## T

$T_0 = 2$, and 
$T_n = T_{n-1} + 3, \forall n > 0$

But what does this function *mean*? We need a closed form!!

## T

But how can we be sure our closed form is correct?

Claim: The closed form solution to the recurrence $T_0 = 2$ and $T_n = T_{n-1} + 3, \forall n > 0$ is $T_n = 2 + 3n$

::: notes
Consider an arbitrary $n$ and the given recurrence.

IH: Assume $\forall j < n, T_j = 2 + 3j$.

Note that either $n = 0$ (base case) or $n > 0$ inductive case.

Case 1: $(n=0)$ The recurrence gives $T_0 = 2$, and the closed form gives $T_0 = 3\cdot 0 + 2 = 2$

Case 2: $(n > 0)$ The recurrence gives $T_n = T_{n-1} + 3$. But from the IH, we know $T_{n-1} = 3(n-1) + 2$. We substitute to get $T_n= [3(n-1) + 2] + 3 = 3n+2$. 
:::
